main_text.p: V. Recta-Ratio est congruum & universale humanarum facultatum testimonium, seu est naturalis humanarum facultatum in verum, honestum & utile inclinatio : Cujus regula est, omne intelligibile, volibile & possibile, seu omne id quod est intellectui, voluntati & facultati executivæ congruè applicatæ congruum, est concedendum ; Hanc qui negat, se esse hominem negat.
VI. Principia experientiā & recta Ratione nixa sunt efficacissima & utilissima in Summis etiam mysteriis cognoscendis, & vere insaniunt qui eorum usum in Theologia rident.
VII. Theosophiæ partes duæ sunt, prior de Deo cognoscendo, posterior de eodem colendo.

page.notes: No marginal notes of this page are legible; the left strip belongs to the neighbouring page edge. Italic and roman distinctions in the first and third paragraphs are approximate. "Theosophiæ" and "duæ" are read from a small, slightly blurred scan and may need checking. Printed "Ca-" is the catchword, cut at the hyphen.
